what_its_for: This medicine is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It combines two medicines in one injection: insulin glargine (a long-acting insulin that lowers blood sugar) and lixisenatide (a medicine that helps your pancreas release insulin after meals and slows digestion). It is used along with diet and exercise to keep your blood sugar in a healthy range.
how_to_take: This medicine is given as an injection under your skin (subcutaneous injection) once a day, within one hour before your first meal of the day. Inject it into your stomach area (abdomen), upper thigh, or upper arm. Rotate your injection sites each day — do not inject in the exact same spot every time. Never inject into a vein or muscle. Use the SoloStar pen that comes with the medicine. Do not mix this medicine with any other insulin or inject it at the same time or place as other injectable medicines. Read the Instructions for Use that come with your pen carefully before starting. Pinch the skin lightly, insert the needle, press the button fully, and hold for 10 seconds before removing the needle. Always use a new needle for each injection.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your blood sugar levels and other medicines you take. Doses are measured in units using the SoloStar pen, which delivers between 15 and 60 units per injection. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first. If you are switching from another insulin or diabetes medicine, your doctor will guide you on how to adjust your dose safely.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip the missed dose and take your next scheduled dose the following day before your first meal. Do not take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist for guidance.
storage: Before first use: Store your unused pens in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Do not freeze this medicine — throw it away if it has been frozen. After first use (in-use pen): Keep the pen at room temperature, below 77°F (25°C), away from heat and light. Do not put the in-use pen back in the refrigerator. Throw away the in-use pen 14 days after first use, even if there is medicine left in it. Always put the cap back on the pen when not in use. Keep the pen and all medicines out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can cause your blood sugar to drop too low or rise unexpectedly. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery if you feel dizzy, confused, or have signs of low blood sugar. Avoid skipping meals after taking your dose, as this can lead to low blood sugar. Do not share your pen, needles, or syringes with anyone else — this can spread infections. Avoid exposing the pen to direct sunlight or extreme heat. Do not use this medicine if it looks cloudy, discolored, or contains particles — it should be clear and colorless.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: signs of low blood sugar (hypoglycemia) such as shakiness, sweating, dizziness, fast heartbeat, confusion, blurred vision, or fainting; signs of high blood sugar (hyperglycemia) such as increased thirst, frequent urination, tiredness, or fruity breath; severe stomach pain that does not go away (this could be a sign of pancreatitis); signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, difficulty breathing, or feeling faint; signs of low potassium such as muscle cramps, weakness, or irregular heartbeat; injection site reactions that are severe or do not heal; nausea or vomiting that prevents you from eating. Also tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding.
when_it_works: Insulin glargine starts working within 1 to 2 hours of injection and provides steady blood sugar control over 24 hours. Lixisenatide works quickly after injection to help control blood sugar spikes after your first meal of the day. You may start to see improvements in your blood sugar levels within a few days to weeks, but it may take several weeks of consistent use, along with healthy eating and exercise, to see the full benefit. Keep taking this medicine even if you feel well, as type 2 diabetes often has no noticeable symptoms.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older): Use with caution. Older adults may be at higher risk for low blood sugar. Your doctor will monitor your blood sugar closely and may adjust your dose. Kidney problems: This medicine may not be suitable if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor about any kidney problems before starting. Liver problems: Use with caution in patients with liver disease, as this may affect blood sugar control and how the medicine works. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine is not recommended during pregnancy. Talk to your doctor right away if you become pregnant. It is not known if this medicine passes into breast milk, so discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children under 18 years of age.
